documents.title: Fiber — Express-inspired web framework for Go
documents.description: Fast, minimalist web framework built on Fasthttp. Robust routing, middleware and Next, static files, template engines, WebSocket, SSE, and a zero-allocation context API.
documents.searchText: # fiber {#fiber} is an [express](https://github.com/expressjs/express) inspired **web framework** built on top of [fasthttp](https://github.com/valyala/fasthttp), the fastest http engine for [go](https://go.dev/doc/). designed to **ease** things up **fast** development with **zero memory allocation** and **performance** in mind. requires **go version `1.26` or higher** run. ## what you get {#what-you-get} - **robust routing** — see [routing context](/sourcey/guides/routing-context.html). **middleware & `next`** chain handlers, logger, cors, recover [middleware](/sourcey/guides/middleware.html). **static files** serve a directory single file [static files error handling](/sourcey/guides/static-error-handling.html). values returned from `fiber.ctx` are reused across requests [zero allocation](/sourcey/guides/zero-allocation.html). **template engines** html by default, plus pug, handlebars, mustache, amber more via `github.com/gofiber/template`. **websocket, socket.io, server-sent events** real-time support middleware packages. **rate limiter, csrf, sessions, caching** internal external cover common production needs. **`net/http` compatibility** router accepts existing `net/http` handlers directly [migration limits](/sourcey/guides/migration-limits.html). where start {#where-to-start} new fiber? read [quickstart](/sourcey/quickstart.html) install, your first "hello, world 👋!" server, core concepts. already routing? context](/sourcey/guides/routing-context.html) [middleware](/sourcey/guides/middleware.html) daily api. shipping production? allocation](/sourcey/guides/zero-allocation.html) limits](/sourcey/guides/migration-limits.html) caveats that bite (context reuse, go floor, semantics). api reference {#api-reference} [go api](/sourcey/api.html) tab full `github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3` package, generated package source: 79 types, 30 package-level functions, 367 methods, 271 constants, 64 variables including `app`, `ctx`, `config`, `router`, `route`, `bind`, `cookie`, helpers. documented {#documented-version} this site documents **gofiber/fiber @ 0d4d872** (commit `0d4d872a29e844159a59b0b9f4cd7afab6ec624a`, 26 nov 2026), mit licensed. source links point at exact commit github.

documents.title: Quickstart
documents.description: Install Fiber v3, run your first Hello World server, and learn the core concepts — app, routes, handlers, Listen.
documents.searchText: # quickstart {#quickstart} fiber requires **go version `1.26` or higher** to run. if you need install upgrade go, visit the [official go download page](https://go.dev/dl/). ## {#install} create a new directory for your project, initialize modules, then fiber: ```bash mod init github.com/your/repo get -u github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3 ``` hello, world! {#hello-world} getting started with is easy. here's basic example simple web server that responds "hello, world 👋!" on root path: ```go package main import ( "log" "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3" ) func main() { // app := fiber.new() define route method path '/' app.get("/", func(c fiber.ctx) error send string response client return c.sendstring("hello, 👋!") }) start port 3000 log.fatal(app.listen(":3000")) } run this program, and `http://localhost:3000` in browser see message. core concepts {#core-concepts} introduces of - **app** — `fiber.new()` creates application. optional `fiber.config` tunes it (see `config` [go api](/sourcey/api.html)). **routes** `app.get`, `app.post`, `app.put`, `app.delete`, friends register handlers + path. paths support parameters (`:name`), wildcards (`*`), segments (`:gender?`) [routing context](/sourcey/guides/routing-context.html). **handlers** handler receives `fiber.ctx` returns an `error`. `c.sendstring`, `c.json`, `c.sendstatus`, `c.render` write response. **middleware** `app.use` registers before (or around) routes; call `c.next()` continue chain [middleware](/sourcey/guides/middleware.html). **listen** `app.listen(":3000")` starts server. `log.fatal` surfaces startup errors. next steps {#next-steps} context](/sourcey/guides/routing-context.html) parameters, wildcards, groups, naming. [middleware](/sourcey/guides/middleware.html) `next` chain, logger, cors. [static files handling](/sourcey/guides/static-error-handling.html) serving files, custom 404s, json responses.

documents.title: Routing and context
documents.description: Route parameters, wildcards, optional segments, route naming, and grouping routes into chains with shared middleware.
documents.searchText: # routing and context {#routing-and-context} ## basic {#basic-routing} routes match a method path. paths support named parameters, wildcards, optional segments: ```go package main import ( "fmt" "log" "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3" ) func main() { app := fiber.new() // get /api/register app.get("/api/*", func(c fiber.ctx) error msg fmt.sprintf("✋ %s", c.params("*")) return c.sendstring(msg) => ✋ register }) /flights/lax-sfo app.get("/flights/:from-:to", fmt.sprintf("💸 from: %s, to: c.params("from"), c.params("to")) 💸 lax, sfo /dictionary.txt app.get("/:file.:ext", fmt.sprintf("📃 %s.%s", c.params("file"), c.params("ext")) 📃 dictionary.txt /john/75 app.get("/:name/:age/:gender?", fmt.sprintf("👴 %s is years old", c.params("name"), c.params("age")) 👴 john 75 old log.fatal(app.listen(":3000")) } ``` `c.params` reads the captured values by name (`"*"` for wildcard). `?` suffix makes segment optional. route naming {#route-naming} can be so handlers build urls to them instead of hard-coding paths. see `route.name` route-naming helpers in [go api](/sourcey/api.html) (`app.get` returns registered `route`). grouping into chains {#grouping-routes-into-chains} `app.group` mounts shared prefix (and middleware) set routes: middleware(c log.println("middleware executed") c.next() handler(c c.sendstring("handler response") api app.group("/api", api.get("/hello", handler) /api/hello runs middleware, then handler {#the-context} every receives `fiber.ctx`. it request-scoped reading headers, query values, request body, writing response (`sendstring`, `json`, `sendstatus`, `render`, `redirect`). `ctx` api](/sourcey/api.html). one rule governs everything about `ctx`: its are **not** immutable reused across requests. never keep references past — [zero allocation](/sourcey/guides/zero-allocation.html).

documents.title: Middleware
documents.description: The Use/Next chain, scoping middleware to a prefix, and the bundled logger and CORS middleware.
documents.searchText: # middleware {#middleware} ## and next {#middleware-and-next} `app.use` registers middleware: handlers that run before the matched route. call `c.next()` to continue chain; returning without it stops request there. ```go package main import ( "fmt" "log" "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3" ) func main() { app := fiber.new() // matches any route app.use(func(c fiber.ctx) error fmt.println("🥇 first handler") return c.next() }) all routes starting with /api app.use("/api", func(c fmt.println("🥈 second get /api/list app.get("/api/list", fmt.println("🥉 last c.sendstring("hello, world 👋!") log.fatal(app.listen(":3000")) } ``` a `get /api/list` prints first, second, then handler, in order. registered prefix only runs for under prefix. logger {#logger} bundled logs each request: "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3/middleware/logger" use app.use(logger.new()) define app.get("/", logger!") cors {#cors} enables cross-origin requests default settings: "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3/middleware/cors" settings app.use(cors.new()) c.sendstring("cors enabled!") check by passing domain `origin` header: ```bash curl -h "origin: http://example.com" --verbose http://localhost:3000 more {#more-middleware} fiber ships internal (adaptor, cache, csrf, session, limiter, recover, sse, static, websocket, `middleware/`) external separate repositories. `recover` catches panics so one bad does not take server down. see packages [go api](/sourcey/api.html) project's documentation full list.

documents.title: Static files and error handling
documents.description: Serve a directory or a single file with the static middleware, return a custom 404, and send JSON responses.
documents.searchText: # static files and error handling {#static-files-and-error-handling} ## serving {#serving-static-files} the middleware serves from a directory: ```go package main import ( "log" "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3" "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3/middleware/static" ) func main() { app := fiber.new() // serve "./public" directory app.get("/*", static.new("./public")) => http://localhost:3000/js/script.js http://localhost:3000/css/style.css app.get("/prefix*", http://localhost:3000/prefix/js/script.js http://localhost:3000/prefix/css/style.css single file for any unmatched routes app.get("*", static.new("./public/index.html")) http://localhost:3000/any/path/shows/index.html log.fatal(app.listen(":3000")) } ``` custom 404 response {#custom-404-response} catch-all registered after all handles paths: define app.get("/", app.get("/demo", func(c fiber.ctx) return c.sendstring("this is demo page!") }) app.post("/register", c.sendstring("registration successful!") to handle not found app.use(func(c c.sendstatus(fiber.statusnotfound) "not found" (the project's readme shows this example without `static` import; above required code compile.) json {#json-response} `c.json` serializes struct or map: type user name string `json:"name"` age int `json:"age"` route that returns object app.get("/user", c.json(&user{"john", 20}) {"name":"john", "age":20} map app.get("/json", c.json(fiber.map{ "success": true, "message": "hi john!", {"success":true, "message":"hi john!"} `fiber.map` `map[string]any` shorthand. status codes are constants such as `fiber.statusnotfound` (404) `fiber.statusok` (200) — see in [go api](/sourcey/api.html).

documents.title: Zero allocation
documents.description: Why Fiber reuses context values across requests, the rule for keeping references, and where the performance claims come from.
documents.searchText: # zero allocation {#zero-allocation} fiber is optimized for **high-performance**, meaning values returned from **`fiber.ctx` are not immutable by default and will be reused across requests**. as a rule of thumb, you **must** only use context within the handler **must not** keep any references. once return handler, obtained in future requests. ## practice {#the-rule-in-practice} ```go app.get("/", func(c fiber.ctx) error { name := c.params("name") // valid: used inside c.sendstring("hello " + name) }) ``` do **not** this: var saved string = wrong: underlying bytes c.sendstring("ok") same applies to request headers, query values, body context: copy them (for example with `utils.copystring`) if they must outlive handler. where numbers come {#where-the-numbers-come-from} fiber's benchmark claims measured [techempower](https://www.techempower.com/benchmarks/#section=data-r19&hw=ph&test=plaintext) (plaintext json rounds). full charts on project's benchmarks pages. framework's speed comes fasthttp plus this reuse discipline — zero-allocation property contract caller, detail callers can ignore. performance checklist {#performance-checklist} - handler; anything that escapes. prefer `c.json` struct over building response strings hand shape fixed. `config` options (`app.config`) tune limits, timeouts, concurrency workload see [go api](/sourcey/api.html).

documents.searchText: # migration and limits {#migration-and-limits} ## migrate from v2 {#migrate-from-v2} coming fiber `v2`? the [fiber cli](https://github.com/gofiber/cli) can your project to `v3` for you. install it, then run `migrate` command in project's directory: ```bash go github.com/gofiber/cli/fiber@latest --to v3 ``` review changes tests afterwards. `fiber --help` see all options, guide documentation what changed `v3`. {#limits} - due fiber's usage of unsafe, library may not always be compatible with latest version. has been tested version 1.26 or higher. automatically adapts common `net/http` handler shapes when you register them on router, still use adaptor middleware need bridge entire apps middleware. net/http compatibility {#nethttp-compatibility} side by standard library. router accepts existing handlers directly even works native `fasthttp.requesthandler` callbacks, so plug legacy endpoints without wrapping manually: ```go package main import ( "log" "net/http" "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v3" ) func main() { httphandler := http.handlerfunc(func(w http.responsewriter, r *http.request) if _, err w.write([]byte("served net/http")); != nil panic(err) } }) app fiber.new() app.get("/", httphandler) // start server port 3000 log.fatal(app.listen(":3000")) convert applications reuse chains, rely it converts middlewares both directions lets mount a server. express-style {#express-style-handlers} also callbacks that operate lightweight `fiber.req` `fiber.res` helper interfaces. this route express-inspired codebases while keeping features: request/response (2-argument) func(req fiber.req, res fiber.res) error return res.sendstring("hello handlers!") an error-returning next callback (3-argument) app.use(func(req fiber.res, func() error) req.ip() == "192.168.1.254" res.sendstatus(fiber.statusforbidden) next() no-arg func()) req.get("x-skip") "true" stop chain calling adapted continue standard-library semantics. they don't get access `fiber.ctx` features incur overhead layer, `fiber.handler` provide best performance.
